notes.title: Freedom Update - GAME IS OPEN SOURCED
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663610/09ed0f9d68e153da0338aaea5379559a849d9412.png

The Game is NOW Open Sourced!

No this is not an late april fools joke, this game is now open source.

I have been working on The Colorful Creature on and off by myself for the past 6 years or so. This game is like a child to me and having the game handed out to people to see and improve it further sounds exciting.

I decided to open source the game as a thanks, and I want to continue to further support the game by giving the community a chance to contribute and improve the game.

For low attention span people, here's the official public repository! View all of it's secrets! 

There's also documentation on how to contribute.

For people who want to report bugs or request features for me or other developers to look at, check the issues tab

What does this mean?

'Open sourcing' any software/game means that the developer(s) are handing out source code entirely for free. It usually requires a license, there's many to choose from but I've chosen Apache 2.0, it means that you can contribute, modify, distribute, or even sell your own version of TCC. It's a legal procedure if I wanted to make the game available to people but I wanted to go on full lengths.

Why did you do this?

For the longest time, I was working on the game by myself, which isn't an issue, but some things took too long to add because of the systems I've implemented that I want to code-refactor, but that takes even longer!

Considering that the game got a full release, I decided to release the game then because I got all of things added that I wanted, but all of these things can be improved in some way.

With me working on other projects, it's difficult to balance TCC and have time for it, I can work on the game but I don't have as much time especially with college and bigger projects planned. So I decided to give the community a chance, with me working on the documentation and help resolve issues with contributors.

I'll be always with the community to help solve issues but now the community can solve the game for me! We can sort the game out together!

Is the game going to be free on steam?

No, the game won't be free on steam, it's just the source code that is becoming free. But you can take the source code and compile the game yourself for free even if you don't own TCC yourself.

There's examples of games that did this, like Cataclysm: Dark Days Ahead where it's sold on steam for 20 euros, but it is free on github.

How can I help

If you don't know how to develop games, or use GameMaker, you don't have to! Head over to the issues tab where you can request bugs and features.

However, if you have any experience with GameMaker, or want to add/fix something, read the contributing.md file and follow instructions. The issues with "good first issue" are easy to add/fix and can get you on the right track.

Keep in mind that the documentation for contributing is work in progress, many things could change to improve workflow of the game, but it will get easier with time.

What is next?

From now on, you can see all plans publicly on github for each major release. I'll keep adding features but now with the community as well. If you need any help regarding to development of the game, join this discord server.

Thank you so much for your support!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40663610/12d6f000e5238a5e5311fa0a6a70ac851f31b23c.png

Welcome to Release 1.1.0! It's focus is on progression and changes to all steam achievements!

Overhauled Achievements
For a while, I was thinking to update the achievements and add brand new ones.

Now, steam doesn't let me add more than 100 achievements to my game. This happens to any game with "Profile Features Limited" on the side of the store page.

The plan is to remove steam achievements that have "Do X amount of things", for example, "Die 10000 times" but instead add something fun like "Beat a week in Calendar" or something, while at the same time, keeping the older achievements still in-game. It's more of a replacement if that makes sense. 

I was also thinking to remove super hard steam achievements like Kaizo and World 7 to encourage players to "100% complete" the game, while at the same time keeping those achievements in-game

So, what does 100% means for the game now?
There is going to be two kinds of 100%s. Steam related and the real 100% completion.

To satisfy speedrunners going for 100%, I'd suggest trying out the steam 100%, because after this update it's likely that the achievements by then won't be changed. As for others who are willing to 100% the game, it would be a very challenging task indeed, but if you pulled it off, hats off to you!

Other things added

 World 7 is nerfed even more
 Other levels will get some minor changes (some levels will be updated to avoid confusion)
 Monthly Endless Run will reset and it will be renamed to 'Seasonal Endless Run', I can't bother to manually reset leaderboards every month lol
 Speaking of Endless Run, brand new levels will be added
 Code will be further improved in some parts of the game
 You will be able to do more things on controller, for example, more menu navigation and changing settings AND SKIPPING LEVELS ON A CONTROLLER

 I'll try to see if I can gather people to contribute to the game's development, as I've opened a google form in the support section

Story of Mark
Once upon a time, a guy called Mark has bought The Colorful Creature

 In the file, below [Other LE], put the following things:
 Workshop Level Version="0"
Publish ID="0"
